assertions.name: three_of_four_are_fkp_hyperbolic
assertions.source: three resolutions attain the FKP hyperbolic form after cyclic reduction, so their closures are hyperbolic

assertions.name: one_of_four_is_undecided
assertions.source: the all-positive resolution is not matched; NOT a proof of non-hyperbolicity, since this test is cyclic rotation only, a proper subset of conjugacy

assertions.name: resolutions_do_NOT_all_agree
assertions.source: so §11.3's optimistic branch — 'if all four agree the ambiguity is harmless' — is NOT available

assertions.name: at_least_three_distinct_conjugacy_classes
assertions.source: exponent sums [1, 3, 5] are distinct; exponent sum is a conjugacy invariant (the abelianisation B_3 -> Z), so the resolutions are genuinely different braids, not presentations of one

assertions.name: matched_forms_escape_the_torus_clause
assertions.source: each matched form carries a strictly negative sigma_2 exponent, so none is conjugate to sigma_1^{p0} sigma_2^{q0} — FKP's excluded torus family — discharging the criterion's negative clause

data.criterion: FKP Thm 5.5 as quoted in library/arxiv-2108.09349v2 §1
data.scope: The test is a SUFFICIENT condition only: it checks cyclic rotations of the reduced word, a proper subset of conjugacy in B_3, and applies no braid relation. A match proves hyperbolic; a non-match proves nothing. Settling the fourth needs a real conjugacy decision procedure (Birman-Ko-Lee / Garside), which is NOT implemented here and is not faked.
